correctness.rationale: A standalone Steiner-symmetrization argument shows that a minimum-area centrally symmetric container may be centered at the dihedral center. Reflection symmetry and constant width then force support value w/2 in the n strip normals, so the centered symmetric hull is exactly the regular 2n-gon conv{±v_j}. Firey's materially inspected area formula simplifies to the numerator used in the ratio. The packaged standard-library checker verifies the strip indexing, polygon area, source-formula simplification, ratio, and monotonicity for odd n=3,...,101; the universal statement rests on the symbolic proof, not the finite replay.

value.rationale: Regular Reuleaux polygons are a canonical comparison family in the established literature on asymmetry of constant-width bodies. The classical Estermann measure is natural on exactly this class, yet the inspected sources provide the triangle extremal statement or other asymmetry measures rather than an all-order profile. The theorem identifies the actual minimizing symmetric hull and gives a closed formula with asymptotic convergence to the disk, supplying a reusable exact benchmark rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
